title: Unit 1: Prompt Structure, Role, Constraints & Output Formatting

topics.title: Output Formatting and Structural Constraints
topics.starter_question: When you write a prompt, how do you specify the exact format and structure you want the model to respond in?

expectations.text: Explicitly specify target format schema (e.g., JSON schema, markdown table, bullet points) to constrain the output distribution.
Use clear boundary delimiters (e.g., XML tags, triple backticks) to separate instructions from user input variables.
Define a system persona or domain role to establish appropriate vocabulary, depth, and tone.

misconceptions.label: Assuming the LLM infers desired output format without explicit instructions
misconceptions.description: Believing vague one-line prompts guarantee consistent, deterministic response structure across runs.

misconceptions.label: Assuming longer prompts automatically produce better outputs without structural constraints
misconceptions.description: Adding conversational adjectives and verbosity instead of well-defined schema rules and negative constraints.

topics.title: System Instructions vs. User Data Separation
topics.starter_question: How do you ensure that dynamic user input does not override or hijack the core system rules in your prompt?

expectations.text: Clearly isolate untrusted user data within dedicated delimiter tags distinct from system instructions.
State defensive boundary instructions that dictate fallback behavior if user inputs conflict with system policy.

misconceptions.label: Treating user input as authoritative system instructions
misconceptions.description: Assuming the model natively distinguishes between system developer intent and arbitrary user strings without structural separation.
